title: Innovation Hubs, Sandboxes and Investment Promotion
summary: How governments attract digital asset business without compromising standards, the design of innovation hubs and sandboxes, and the reputational risks of competing on light-touch regulation.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How governments attract digital asset business without compromising standards, the design of innovation hubs and sandboxes, and the reputational risks of competing on light-touch regulation.
Learning Objectives: Distinguish innovation hubs, regulatory sandboxes and accelerator programmes
Evaluate the economic case and the reputational risks of attracting digital asset firms
Define the respective roles of ministries, promotion agencies and regulators
Syllabus: Innovation hub and sandbox design: eligibility, safeguards and exit
Attracting firms: licensing speed, standards and the race to the bottom
Case studies of financial centre strategies and their consequences
Protecting regulatory independence in investment promotion
Intended Audience: Officials in finance ministries and treasuries developing digital asset, fintech and innovation policy
Legislative drafters, legal advisers and parliamentary committee staff working on digital asset legislation
Staff of investment promotion agencies, innovation offices and other public bodies engaging with the digital asset sector
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some familiarity with financial services policy is helpful. No technical background in blockchain or computing is required.
Core Reading: FSB (2023), Global Regulatory Framework for Crypto-Asset Activities
FSB (2023), High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Global Stablecoin Arrangements
IOSCO (2023), Policy Recommendations for Crypto and Digital Asset Markets
FATF (2021), Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers
OECD (2022), Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework and Amendments to the Common Reporting Standard
